title: Preserve set semantics for iterator operands and repeated XOR values
body:
## The change

`IndexedSet` now preserves set semantics when intersection, difference or symmetric difference receives a one-shot iterator. Membership checks previously consumed the operand, and symmetric difference reused an exhausted iterator. In-place XOR also toggled duplicate values repeatedly and skipped values when given an iterator over itself.

Snapshot iterator operands before repeated membership checks and deduplicate in-place XOR inputs. Reusable set/list operands retain their existing membership behavior. Existing output ordering is preserved.

Five regressions fail before the change. The full suite and module doctests pass afterward: **677 passed** on Python 3.11.15. This does not duplicate PR494, which corrects multi-operand intersection/difference update semantics.

## The backstory

This continues the explicitly AI-assisted utility-library investigation described in #502. These cases compare the public set-like API with Python's built-in set operations using ordinary one-shot iterables; they were not discovered in production usage.

## AI assistance

- Harness/tooling: OpenAI Codex acting on behalf of rupayon123.
- Model: GPT-6-based Codex; exact backend variant not exposed.
- Original task excerpt: “Execute my daily GitHub contribution and maintenance workflow on my behalf. Do real, verified work, not only research, a plan, configuration changes, or a status summary.” The task requires reproducible fixes, duplicate checking, and appropriate validation before submission.
